evidence.why: Aligned bodies are compiler-conditional; alignment peeling subtracts its count without validating the supplied length.
Unaligned bodies show compiler guards, complementary shifts, aligned neighboring-word reads and unconditional paired-word bulk loops.
Caller establishes minimum length, address-order direction and relative-alignment selection before forwarding all three arguments.

facts.rationale: Adds useful compiler-branch, input-contract and source-access qualifications absent from the existing stage summaries, without changing their supported account of normal caller-driven copying.
facts.value: All four workers return without copying when __MWERKS__ is undefined. Their operative target implementations rely on specialized caller preconditions rather than validating arbitrary inputs: memmove supplies at least 32 bytes and selects direction and relative alignment. In particular, both unaligned workers execute a do-while bulk loop with initial count n >> 3 after alignment peeling, without a zero-count guard. Differing modulo-four alignment keeps src_offset nonzero, avoiding the zero-offset case that would compute a 32-bit right shift. Their adjacent aligned source-word loads may encompass bytes outside the logical source interval; the requested destination interval is the output, not a bound on every source load.
